reran: cmd.sh on w4-int, w3-base and 2.13.18: FatalError 'mergePrefixAndArgs(List(ErasedValueType(class V0, Int), ErasedValueType(class V0, Int(7))), covariant, Depth(1)): unsupported tps' during erasure on all three. Scala 3.7.4 compiles the variants I tried. With JDK 17: 2.10.7 compiles it; 2.11.0, 2.11.12, 2.12.20, 2.13.0 and 2.13.10 crash.
user_impact: Any if or match yielding a value class where one branch passes a literal or constant (including a final val constant) to the constructor and the other a non-constant, used directly as the receiver of ==, !=, or a field accessor: (if (ok) Meters(d) else Meters(0)).value or (if (c) Id(n) else Id(Zero)) == other. Plain code with a default value in one branch, not an artificial input. Vals of the value class in both branches, binding the conditional to a val first, an argument position, equals/hashCode/toString, and a user method of the value class (all rewritten to extension-method calls with the conditional as argument) are fine.
fixability: clear cut: in the InjectDerivedValue case of Eraser.typed1, give the tree ErasedValueType(tref.sym, result.tpe.widen) (or deconst) so two injections of the same class agree; V0(7: Int) avoids the crash, which supports this. No binary or behaviour cost.
regression: in 2.11.0: 4acac088dc (SI-6385, scala/scala PR 3082, 2.11.0-M7) changed ErasedValueType from the class's type ref to (class, underlying), and the InjectDerivedValue case has since passed the argument's unwidened type as the underlying; 2.10.7 compiles the program.
links: No ticket found in scala/bug (mergePrefixAndArgs, unsupported tps, ErasedValueType queries) or the local Scala index. No wave-one to wave-three finding (VC*, UM*, EL*) touches the InjectDerivedValue type or lub of ErasedValueTypes. Neighbour, not duplicate: retronym/scala#427 teaches -Ycheck about the same InjectDerivedValue trees.
note: Mechanism confirmed with -Vdebug: no value-class rewrite of == is involved. Erasure re-types the Select qualifier with pt=?, typedIf/typedMatch then takes the lub of the branch types, and lub cannot merge ErasedValueType(V0, Int) with ErasedValueType(V0, Int(7)) because the injection's type carries the constant type of its argument. Both branches the same literal compiles (identical types); two different literals crash; new V0(7) without the case-class apply crashes; a block {if ...}.u crashes; a String-wrapping class with a "" literal and a generic class G[T] over a String literal crash; G[Int] with an Int literal is fine because the literal is boxed to Object. The finding's 'used as a receiver' is right but narrower than stated: receivers of members that extmethods turns into extension calls do not crash.
